This directly supports the rule regarding the alignment of Functional Status Sets on a 32-bit boundary, confirming both the existence and the correctness of the rule as extracted.
rules.test_hint: Generate messages with Functional Status Sets misaligned to test alignment enforcement
rules.source_quote: Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.

rules.name: String Data 2-byte Boundary Alignment
rules.consensus_value: address % 2 == 0
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that for data primitives whose length can vary, such as a string, padding should be used to put the data on a 2-byte boundary (address evenly divisible by 2). This aligns with the extracted rule regarding string data alignment.
rules.test_hint: Create messages with variable-length strings not aligned on 2-byte boundaries to test alignment handling
rules.source_quote: For data primitives whose length can vary, such as a string, it would not be acceptable to expect its address to be divisible by its length as its length could get very large. In cases such as this, padding should be used to put the data on a 2-byte boundary (address evenly divisible by 2).

rules.name: Data primitives placement constraint
rules.consensus_value: Data primitives must be placed one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The text clearly mentions that 'Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.' This matches the rule's constraint value exactly.
rules.test_hint: Create frames with gaps between data primitives that are not alignment padding and verify network behavior
rules.source_quote: Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.

rules.name: Unused spare field fill value
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused. This aligns with the extracted rule that specifies the allowed value for unused spare fields as 0.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in unused spare fields and verify network behavior
rules.source_quote: Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.

rules.name: Reserved field fill value
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that the 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros, confirming the rule as genuine. The extracted value of 0 is correct as it aligns with the requirement for binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in the 32-bit reserved field and verify network behavior
rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: Global spare field fill value
rules.justification: The specification text clearly states that if the Global Spare field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros. This matches the rule's constraint that the allowed value is 0.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in the global spare field and verify network behavior
rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.name: Parameter removal replacement rule
rules.consensus_value: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly outlines that when a parameter is removed from a data set, it should be replaced with a pad and not cause a shift in the remainder of the message. This aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Generate messages where parameters are removed without proper padding, or where message structure shifts after parameter removal
rules.source_quote: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.

rules.name: Minimize message impact on parameter insertion
rules.consensus_value: Minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields.
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The guideline to 'minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields' is directly quoted from the specification.
rules.test_hint: Generate messages where new parameters are inserted in ways that shift existing parameter positions instead of using spare/pad fields
rules.source_quote: Minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields.

rules.name: Byte order in data primitives
rules.consensus_value: The boxes that represent a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, the most significant byte on the left, the least significant byte on the right.
rules.justification: The rule regarding byte order in data primitives is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification mentions that the boxes representing a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, with the most significant byte on the left and the least significant byte on the right. This directly aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Generate messages with incorrect byte order (LSB first instead of MSB first) to test parsing behavior
rules.source_quote: The boxes that represent a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, the most significant byte on the left, the least significant byte on the right.

rules.name: Bit order within bytes
rules.consensus_value: The bits in the bytes are most significant bit on the left and least significant bit on the right.
rules.justification: The rule about bit order within bytes is explicitly stated in the specification text. The quote provided in the rule matches the text in the specification, confirming that the most significant bit is on the left and the least significant bit is on the right within bytes.
rules.test_hint: Generate messages with incorrect bit ordering within bytes to test bit-level parsing behavior
rules.source_quote: Also, the bits in the bytes are most significant bit on the left and least significant bit on the right.

rules.name: Single ARINC 429 Label Message Structure
rules.consensus_value: Single ARINC 429 labels must be placed in fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive with FS status field
rules.justification: The specification text in Appendix B clearly states that a single ARINC 429 label should be placed in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive, which aligns with the extracted rule. The FS status field is also mentioned as part of the structure for single label messages.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with ARINC 429 single labels that don't follow the 32-bit fixed length structure or are missing the FS status field
rules.source_quote: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive

rules.name: Multiple ARINC 429 Labels Concentration
rules.consensus_value: Multiple ARINC 429 labels can be placed in variable length opaque structure with appropriate DS fields
rules.justification: The specification text in Appendix B describes the integration of multiple ARINC 429 labels into a variable length opaque structure, which aligns with the rule's constraint. The text explicitly mentions placing a varying number of labels in a variable length opaque structure, confirming the rule's validity.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with multiple ARINC 429 labels that don't use proper variable length opaque structure or have incorrect DS field associations
rules.source_quote: Place a varying number of labels in a variable length opaque structure

rules.name: Variable Length Structure Maximum Size
rules.consensus_value: Maximum size of variable length opaque structure must be established from maximum number of labels that could arrive between transmissions and statically configured
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text describes the need for the system designer to determine the maximum number of labels that could arrive at the gateway between transmissions. This maximum number is used to establish the maximum size of the variable length opaque structure, which is then statically configured into the system.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with variable length structures that exceed the statically configured maximum size or use dynamic sizing instead of static configuration
rules.source_quote: The system designer must figure out what the highest or maximum number of labels is that could possibly arrive at the gateway between transmissions. From this maximum number the maximum size of the variable length opaque structure is established. This structure is then statically configured into the system

rules.name: Variable Length Field Population
rules.consensus_value: Labels must be placed sequentially after length and pad fields, length field must contain actual byte count of valid data, unused portion filled with binary zeros
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly described in the specification text. The text outlines the process of placing labels sequentially after the length and pad fields, computing the length of valid data, and filling unused portions with binary zeros. This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames where labels aren't placed sequentially, length field doesn't match actual data size, or unused portions contain non-zero data
rules.source_quote: As labels arrive at the gateway, they are placed one after another in the opaque structure beginning with the byte after the length field and pad field. When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure. The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros

rules.name: Static length allocation for wrapped ARINC 429 messages
rules.justification: The specification text in Appendix B explicitly mentions 'Static Length = 40 bytes' for the ARINC 429 to AFDX formatting, confirming the rule about static length allocation for wrapped ARINC 429 messages.
rules.test_hint: Generate AFDX frames with wrapped ARINC 429 messages that deviate from the 40-byte static length allocation
rules.source_quote: Static Length = 40 bytes

rules.name: Dynamic length for ARINC 429 data structure
rules.justification: The specification text in Appendix B mentions a 'Dynamic Length = 22' in the context of ARINC 429 data structure formatting. This matches the rule's description and constraint value.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with ARINC 429 data that claims dynamic length of 22 bytes but contains different actual data lengths
rules.source_quote: Dynamic Length = 22

rules.name: IPv4 Version Requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which requires the packet structure version to be IPv4. The extracted value is correct as it aligns with the specification.
rules.test_hint: Send packets with IP version field set to values other than 4 (e.g., IPv6 version 6)
rules.source_quote: The packet structure version should be IPv4.

rules.name: IPv4 Packet Structure Compliance
rules.consensus_value: Must comply with specified IPv4 packet structure format
rules.justification: The specification clearly states that the IPv4 packet structure should comply with Figure 3-30, which outlines the specific format for IPv4 packets. This aligns with the rule's requirement for compliance with the specified IPv4 packet structure format.
rules.test_hint: Send packets with incorrect IPv4 header field sizes, wrong field order, or missing mandatory fields
rules.source_quote: IPv4 packet structure should be compliant with Figure 3-30.

rules.name: IPv4 Total Length Field Range in AFDX
rules.justification: The rule regarding the IPv4 Total Length field range in AFDX is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text specifies that ordinarily, the range is from 21 to 1500 bytes, but in AFDX, it is from 21 to 1499 bytes due to the Sequence Number. This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send IPv4 packets with Total Length field set to values outside the range 21-1499 bytes (e.g., 20, 1500, or larger values)
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number

rules.name: Unique Data Flow Identification
rules.consensus_value: Must be uniquely identified by UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, MAC destination address, and physical Ethernet connections
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The source quote matches the rule's description, confirming that a data flow is uniquely identified by the set of UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, MAC destination address, and physical Ethernet connections.
rules.test_hint: Create flows with duplicate combinations of these identifiers to test uniqueness enforcement
rules.source_quote: A data flow is uniquely identified within AFDX network by the set of UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, MAC destination address and the physical Ethernet connection(s) of the receiving ES.

rules.name: Valid Frame Filtering Criteria
rules.consensus_value: Must filter frames based on destination TCP/UDP addresses, IP addresses, MAC addresses, and physical Ethernet connections
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification text, which states that frame-based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. The validity of a frame is defined by the analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect destination addresses or on wrong physical connections to test filtering behavior
rules.source_quote: Frame based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. Valid frame being defined by analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.

rules.name: Switched Ethernet Network Requirement
rules.consensus_value: AFDX networks must be implemented as switched Ethernet networks
rules.justification: The specification text in section 2.2 discusses the use of switched Ethernet networks as a model for deterministic networks, which aligns with the rule stating that AFDX networks must be implemented as switched Ethernet networks. This is a fundamental aspect of AFDX network architecture.
rules.test_hint: This is an architectural requirement that cannot be violated by frame generation
rules.source_quote: Switched Ethernet Networks

rules.name: AFDX network communication with wider profiled networks
rules.consensus_value: A deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The source quote matches the rule's constraint value, confirming that a deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways.
rules.test_hint: Test gateway behavior by sending frames between deterministic and profiled network segments to verify proper routing and protocol translation
rules.source_quote: A deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways.

rules.name: Constant message delivery time in point-to-point system
rules.consensus_value: message delivery time through network from emitter to receiver is constant
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text mentions that since the bandwidth is fixed, there are no collisions, and the end system latency is constant, the time taken to deliver a message through the network from the emitter to the receiver is constant. This aligns with the rule's description of constant message delivery time in a point-to-point system.
rules.test_hint: Measure delivery times for identical messages and verify they are constant, or introduce conditions that would cause timing variation
rules.source_quote: Since the bandwidth is fixed, there are no collisions, and the end system latency is constant, the time taken to deliver a message, through the network, from the emitter to the receiver is constant

rules.name: No Continuous Gateway Pinging
rules.consensus_value: no_continuous_pinging_allowed
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously. This aligns with the extracted rule regarding 'No Continuous Gateway Pinging'.
rules.test_hint: Generate continuous ping traffic to gateways and verify this behavior is not implemented or is rejected
rules.source_quote: hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously

rules.name: Conditional Pinging Only When Sending Traffic
rules.consensus_value: ping_only_when_traffic_being_sent_and_no_positive_indication
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text mentions that 'Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway… and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.' This aligns with the rule's constraint of 'ping_only_when_traffic_being_sent_and_no_positive_indication.'
rules.test_hint: Send ping packets when no traffic is being transmitted or when positive gateway indications exist, verify this violates the constraint
rules.source_quote: Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway...and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning

rules.name: System Scalability
rules.consensus_value: AFDX networks are designed to scale to accommodate a large number of end systems and virtual links.
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions that the choice of network topology, specifically the cascaded star topology, impacts the scalability of the AFDX system design. This supports the rule that AFDX networks are designed to scale to accommodate a large number of end systems and virtual links.
rules.source_quote: 2.3 Scalability

rules.name: Default physical port designation
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification clearly mentions that Port #1 is the default external physical port used to communicate with the End System of the Switch.
rules.source_quote: Port # 1 is the default external physical port used to communicate with the End System of the Switch.

rules.name: Default port speed configuration
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that the default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Send frames at different speeds or with auto-negotiation enabled to test if switch rejects non-100Mbps configurations
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: port_speed_options
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text in section 4.11.2 clearly mentions that each port speed should be configurable to operate at speeds of 10 Mbps or 100 Mbps in full duplex, without auto negotiation. The extracted values and constraints match the specification.
rules.test_hint: Configure ports with speeds other than 10 or 100 Mbps or enable auto-negotiation
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: full_duplex_requirement
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that each port speed should be configurable to operate at speeds of 10 Mbps or 100 Mbps in full duplex, without auto negotiation. This confirms that full duplex is a requirement for the duplex mode.
rules.test_hint: Configure ports in half-duplex mode
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: auto_negotiation_disabled
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that each port speed should be configurable to operate at speeds of 10 Mbps or 100 Mbps in full duplex, without auto negotiation. This confirms the rule that auto negotiation should be disabled.
rules.test_hint: Enable auto-negotiation on switch ports
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: Default port speed
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The default port speed is indeed specified as 100 Mbps without auto negotiation in section 4.7.2.1.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure the port speed to a value other than 100 Mbps.
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.

rules.name: Port Number Range
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that transport layer port assignments can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535. This matches the rule's constraint on the port number range.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic using port numbers outside the range 1 to 65535 to test how the network handles invalid port numbers.
rules.source_quote: Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.

rules.name: SAP Port Transmission Binding Uniqueness
rules.consensus_value: single binding per SAP port to one (UDP port source, IP source, VL MAC destination) tuple
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification text in section 3.4.1.5.2, which states that in transmission, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source, and VL (MAC destination)). This matches the extracted rule's constraint value.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple transmission bindings for the same SAP port with different UDP source ports, IP sources, or VL destinations
rules.source_quote: In transmission, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source and VL (MAC destination)).

rules.name: SAP Port Reception Binding Uniqueness
rules.consensus_value: single binding per SAP port to one (UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination, VL MAC destination) tuple
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 3.4.1.5.2. It specifies that in reception, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set consisting of a UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination, and VL (MAC destination). This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple reception bindings for the same SAP port with different UDP/TCP destination ports, IP destinations, or VL destinations
rules.source_quote: In reception, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination and VL (MAC destination))

rules.name: Well-known Port Range
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that the port range 0-1023 is administered by ICANN and designated as 'Well-known' port numbers. This matches the rule's constraint and source quote.

rules.source_quote: 0 – 1023 Administered by ICANN "Well-known" port number

rules.name: Standard Communication Port Range
rules.justification: The rule regarding the port range for standard communications is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text mentions that the port range 0-1023 is used for standard communications, which aligns with the extracted rule.

rules.name: SAP Bidirectional Communication Port Range
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that the port range 1024 to 65535 is used for bi-directional communication, specifically mentioning SAP AFDX and compliant networks. This matches the rule's constraint value.

rules.name: Fault Isolation in Switch
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions that for the system to maintain maximum integrity in the event of a fault on either ESa or ESb, the Quality of Service (QoS) definition may include continued delivery of data from the non-faulty node. This implies a method of fault isolation in the switch, which aligns with the rule's description.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a fault in one end system and check if the switch continues to deliver data from the non-faulty node.
rules.source_quote: For the system to maintain maximum integrity in the event of a fault on either ESa or ESb, the Quality of Service (QoS) definition may include continued delivery of data from the non-faulty node.

rules.name: Required Protocol Support
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed as genuine because the specification text in section 1.2 Scope explicitly lists the required protocols for interoperable functional elements, which match the values in the rule.
rules.test_hint: Test by sending frames that use unsupported or incorrectly implemented required protocols and verify proper handling or rejection
rules.source_quote: The requirements listed in this document aim at specifying interoperable functional elements: Data link: MAC, VL addressing concept; Network: IP, ICMP; Transport: UDP, TCP (optional); Network application layers: Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP and SNMP

rules.name: TCP Optional Support
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions that TCP is optional in the transport layer, as stated in the rule. The rule correctly identifies TCP support as optional, which aligns with the specification's allowance for TCP as an optional protocol.
rules.test_hint: Test by sending TCP frames to devices that may not support TCP and verify graceful handling or appropriate rejection
rules.source_quote: Transport: UDP, TCP (optional)

rules.name: Maximum Network Transit Delay Guarantee
rules.consensus_value: maximum network transit delay must be guaranteed for each transmission
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that each network transmission request must be serviced regardless of the data type and a maximum network transit delay must be guaranteed. This aligns with the rule's constraint that a maximum network transit delay must be guaranteed for each transmission.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic loads that could cause transit delays to exceed guaranteed maximums
rules.source_quote: Each network transmission request must be serviced regardless of the data type and a maximum network transit delay (also called end-to-end latency) must be guaranteed.

rules.name: Guaranteed Bandwidth Requirement
rules.consensus_value: guaranteed service must provide constant bandwidth at link level
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that a guaranteed service provides both an upper bounded delay and constant bandwidth, which aligns with the extracted rule about guaranteed bandwidth at the link level.
rules.test_hint: Create conditions where bandwidth allocation varies or is not guaranteed
rules.source_quote: Hence a guaranteed service provides both upper bounded delay and constant bandwidth leading to a logical open connection

rules.name: FIFO discipline requirement
rules.justification: The rule regarding the FIFO discipline requirement for message ordering in the queuing service is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that 'To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.' This matches the extracted rule exactly.
rules.test_hint: Implement LIFO or random message ordering instead of FIFO
rules.source_quote: To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.

rules.name: Maximum application data size
rules.justification: The rule about the maximum application data size for the queuing service is explicitly stated in the specification. The text mentions that each instance of the Queuing Service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets of application data, which corresponds to 8192 bytes, and that IP fragmentation is needed for this purpose.
rules.test_hint: Send queuing service messages larger than 8192 bytes
rules.source_quote: Each instance of Queuing Service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets of application data (IP fragmentation is thus needed).

rules.name: In-order fragment transmission
rules.justification: The rule regarding in-order fragment transmission is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 3.3.1.1.2.1. The text clearly mentions that when fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network, which aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Transmit fragments out-of-order to the AFDX network
rules.source_quote: When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.

rules.name: Buffer overflow frame discard
rules.consensus_value: discard_frame_and_send_error_indication
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 3.3.1.1.2.1, which describes the behavior when a buffer overflow occurs during transmission. It specifies that an error indication should be sent to the transmitting partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Continue processing frames after buffer overflow without discarding or sending error indication
rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in transmission, an error indication should be sent to the transmitting partition and the frame should be discarded

rules.name: Handling Frame Loss
rules.consensus_value: Frame from redundant network is accepted if one is lost.
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed as it is directly supported by the specification text. The text explicitly states that when a frame is lost on Network A, the frame arriving on the B Network is accepted. This aligns with the rule's description of redundancy management and fault tolerance in handling frame loss.
rules.test_hint: Simulate loss of frames on one network and ensure frames from the redundant network are accepted.
rules.source_quote: Redundancy management result: The frame arriving on the B Network is accepted.

rules.name: First Win Redundancy Delivery
rules.consensus_value: Deliver the first of the redundant frames received
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The text clearly mentions that when redundancy management is active, the system should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple redundant frames and verify that only the first received is delivered.
rules.source_quote: When redundancy management is active, it should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.

rules.name: Reset Tolerance
rules.consensus_value: Reset of any equipment should not affect redundancy management
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed as it is explicitly stated in the specification text that a reset of any equipment involved in the communication should not affect redundancy management. The extracted value accurately reflects this requirement.
rules.test_hint: Perform a reset on network devices and ensure redundancy management continues unaffected.
rules.source_quote: Reset of any equipment involved in the communication (transmitting End system, receiving End system or the AFDX switch) should not affect this property.

rules.name: Data presentation after reassembly
rules.consensus_value: No data should be presented until whole message is reassembled
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 3.3.1.1.2.2. It clearly mentions that no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until the whole message has been reassembled, which matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented frames and check if data is presented before reassembly.
rules.source_quote: In case of fragmentation, no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until whole message has been reassembled.

rules.name: Buffer overflow handling
rules.consensus_value: Send error message and discard frame on buffer overflow
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 3.3.1.1.2.2, which describes the behavior required when a buffer overflow occurs in reception. The specification clearly states that an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Cause buffer overflow and check if error message is sent and frame is discarded.
rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.

rules.name: Redundancy Management Requirement
rules.consensus_value: Receiving End Systems must implement redundancy management mechanisms
rules.justification: The specification text describes the redundancy management mechanism in detail, including the 'First Valid wins' policy and the role of redundancy management in eliminating duplicate frames. This aligns with the rule stating that receiving end systems must implement redundancy management mechanisms.
rules.test_hint: Send duplicate frames on redundant paths with conflicting data or timing
rules.source_quote: Redundancy Management

rules.name: Dual network transmission
rules.consensus_value: In default mode each frame is sent across both of two networks
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that in default mode, each frame is sent across both networks, which aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on only one network instead of both networks to violate redundancy requirement
rules.source_quote: In default mode each frame is sent across both of two networks.

rules.name: Duplicate frame discard
rules.consensus_value: When the second frame is received with this sequence number, it is simply discarded
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text describes the redundancy management process, where frames are sent across both networks, and the 'First Valid wins' policy is applied. The first frame with the next valid sequence number is accepted, and any subsequent frame with the same sequence number is discarded, which matches the rule description.
rules.test_hint: Send duplicate frames with same sequence number and verify second frame is discarded
rules.source_quote: When the second frame is received with this sequence number, it is simply discarded.

rules.name: Redundancy management after integrity checking
rules.consensus_value: RM (Redundancy Management) is placed after IC (Integrity Checking)
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly indicates that Redundancy Management (RM) is placed after Integrity Checking (IC) as part of the frame processing order. This matches the extracted rule and its value.
rules.source_quote: As the flow of frames given in Figure3-14 below indicates, RM (Redundancy Management) is placed after IC (Integrity Checking).

rules.name: Maximum time difference between redundant frames
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that redundant copies of a frame should be sent within a maximum time difference of 0.5 ms to simplify the algorithm on the receiving End System.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames with time difference greater than 0.5ms
rules.source_quote: In order to simplify the algorithm on the receiving End System, redundant copies of a frame should be sent within a maximum time difference of 0.5 ms.

rules.name: Per-VL redundancy configuration capability
rules.consensus_value: ES must be configurable per VL to send messages on either or both networks
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that on a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks and that this property should be configurable.
rules.test_hint: Test ES behavior when VL is configured for single network but frames are sent on both networks
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks. This property should be configurable.

rules.name: Redundant VL single data delivery mode
rules.consensus_value: ES must be able to receive redundant VL and deliver only one copy of redundant data to partition when RM active
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification mentions that on a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive a redundant VL and deliver to the partition one of the redundant data when RM is active. This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames and verify only one copy is delivered to partition when RM is active
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition one of the redundant data (RM active)

rules.name: Redundant VL dual data delivery mode
rules.consensus_value: ES must be able to receive redundant VL and deliver both copies of redundant data to partition when RM not active
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text mentions that on a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive a redundant VL and deliver both redundant data to the partition when RM is not active.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames and verify both copies are delivered to partition when RM is not active
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition both redundant data (RM not active)

rules.name: Non-redundant VL reception capability
rules.consensus_value: ES must be able to receive non-redundant VL on either interface and submit data to partition regardless of RM state
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification mentions that on a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive a non-redundant VL on either interface and submit data from it to the partition, regardless of whether RM is active or not.
rules.test_hint: Send non-redundant frames on single interface and verify proper delivery regardless of RM configuration
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A non redundant VL on either interface and submit data from it to the partition (in this case, RM can be active or not)

rules.name: First Win Frame Delivery
rules.consensus_value: deliver_first_received_redundant_frame
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that when redundancy management is active, the system should deliver the first of the redundant frames received. This aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames with different arrival times and verify only the first received is delivered, or send frames out of order to test if later frames are incorrectly accepted
rules.source_quote: When redundancy management is active, it should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.

rules.name: Reset Persistence
rules.consensus_value: first_win_property_maintained_after_reset
rules.warning: Found by only one model, not yet verified

rules.name: Copy Frame Loss Due to Sequencing
rules.consensus_value: copy_frame_lost_if_out_of_sequence_after_faster_network_advance
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification text, which describes the behavior of the Redundancy Management function in handling frames that are out of sequence. The text explicitly states that the loss of one frame on one network could lead to the loss of its copy if it arrives out of sequence after the network has already advanced. This aligns with the extracted rule about copy frame loss due to sequencing.
rules.test_hint: Create scenarios where one network is faster than another and verify that late-arriving copies are dropped when the sequence has already advanced
rules.source_quote: As a consequence, in some cases, the loss of one frame on one network could also lead to the loss of its copy.

rules.name: Single DS for Single Threaded Concentrator
rules.consensus_value: If all labels are concentrated by single threaded device, single DS should be used with DS status reflected by single FS
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that if all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS. This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames from single threaded concentrators that incorrectly use multiple DS fields or have inconsistent FS-DS relationships
rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS

rules.name: Multiple DS for Partial Failure Scenarios
rules.consensus_value: If concentrator can have partial failures affecting some labels while generating valid frame, multiple DS should be used with each DS having own FS
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text describes a scenario where a concentrator device may experience partial failures affecting some labels, yet still generate a valid Ethernet frame. In such cases, the specification advises using multiple DS (Data Structures), each with its own FS (Frame Status), to ensure that valid data can still be received and used despite the presence of faults. This aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with partial failures where DS assignments don't properly isolate failed from valid labels, or FS fields don't correctly represent their respective DS status
rules.source_quote: If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail in some way that causes some labels to be invalid, but a completely legal Ethernet frame is still generated with some valid labels, more than one DS should be considered. This way each DS is represented by its own FS

rules.name: Sampling message size constraint
rules.consensus_value: ≤ VL_payload_size
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that Sampling Com Ports should not use IP fragmentation, and therefore the size of each sampling message should be less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send sampling messages larger than the associated Virtual Link payload size
rules.source_quote: Sampling Com Ports should not use IP fragmentation, therefore the size of each sampling message should be less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link.

rules.name: Sampling service multicast requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that the sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.
rules.test_hint: Configure sampling service to use unicast instead of multicast communication
rules.source_quote: Sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.

rules.name: Sampling service unidirectional requirement
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed as it is directly supported by the specification text. The specification clearly states that the sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors, which aligns with the rule's constraint of 'unidirectional' communication.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to establish bidirectional communication using sampling service
rules.source_quote: Sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.

rules.name: Sampling service no error control
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that the sampling service does not add error control on transmitted data and does not require flow control in addition to the VL flow control. This aligns with the extracted rule indicating that error control is not enabled for the sampling service.
rules.test_hint: Add error control mechanisms to sampling service transmission
rules.source_quote: It does not add error control on transmitted data and does not require flow control in addition to the VL flow control.

rules.name: Multiple partition access to sampling port
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text, which states that the last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions. This implies that multiple partitions can access the same sampling port, aligning with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Block multiple partitions from accessing the same sampling port
rules.source_quote: The last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions (i.e. several partitions may subscribe to this sampling port).

rules.name: Freshness indication requirement
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that a freshness indication should be associated with each sampling port and should be available to each partition reading the message.
rules.test_hint: Remove or disable freshness indication from sampling ports
rules.source_quote: A freshness indication should be associated to each sampling port. This freshness indication should be available to each partition reading the message.

rules.name: Static Route Definition Required
rules.consensus_value: routes_must_be_statically_defined
rules.justification: The specification text states that the addressing for end-to-end communications within the AFDX network is statically defined, which aligns with the rule that routes must be statically defined. This confirms the rule's validity.
rules.test_hint: Attempt dynamic routing operations or expect dynamic route updates when AFDX requires static configuration
rules.source_quote: AFDX is statically defined

rules.name: No Gateway Failure Detection
rules.justification: The specification text indicates that AFDX is statically defined and does not utilize default gateways, which implies that there is no need for gateway failure detection. This aligns with the rule stating 'No Gateway Failure Detection' with a boolean value of false.
rules.test_hint: Test scenarios expecting gateway failure detection or automatic gateway switching when AFDX has no default gateways
rules.source_quote: AFDX is statically defined, no default gateways

rules.name: Default Configuration Table Usage
rules.consensus_value: Defines default behavior of the End System of the Switch
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that the Default_Configuration_Table is used to define the default behavior of the End System of the Switch, including default reception and transmission. This aligns with the rule's description.
rules.test_hint: Test by resetting the switch and verifying that it uses the Default_Configuration_Table for reception and transmission.
rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_Table is used to define the default behavior of the End System of the Switch: default reception and default transmission.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap
rules.consensus_value: Defined per VL
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAGi)' as a parameter required to configure the Filtering, Policing, and Forwarding functions of the Switch on a per VL basis. This aligns with the rule's description of BAG being defined per VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with BAG values outside the configured range for a VL to test policing.
rules.source_quote: Bandwith Allocation Gap (BAGi)

rules.name: Maximum Ethernet Frame Size
rules.consensus_value: Defined per VL
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax)' as a parameter in the switch configuration, confirming the existence of this rule. The rule's description aligns with the specification's mention of 'Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax)' under both reception and transmission VL configurations.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than Smax to test if they are dropped or flagged.
rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet Frame Size
rules.consensus_value: Defined per VL
rules.justification: The rule regarding the 'Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)' is explicitly mentioned in the specification under the section '4.0 SWITCH SPECIFICATION'. It is listed as a parameter that should be configured on a per Virtual Link (VL) basis. The extracted value 'Defined per VL' aligns with the specification's requirement that these parameters are configured per VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than Smin to test if they are dropped or flagged.
rules.source_quote: Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)

rules.name: Maximum Port Delay
rules.consensus_value: Defined per port
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that an output port should not transmit frames that are older than 'max delay,' and that this parameter is defined on a per port basis in the configuration table. This aligns with the rule's description of 'Maximum Port Delay' and its constraint being 'Defined per port.'
rules.test_hint: Introduce delays exceeding the maximum to see if frames are dropped or delayed.
rules.source_quote: Max delay

rules.name: Technological Latency Limit
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote provided matches the text in the specification, confirming that the technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Introduce delays in the switch processing to exceed 100 μs and observe network behavior.
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.

rules.name: Minimum Output Port Buffer Capacity
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames, balanced between high and low priority. This directly matches the rule's constraint and description.
rules.test_hint: Send a burst of frames to an output port to exceed 512 frames and check if frames are dropped.
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).

rules.name: Sub-VL FIFO queue exclusivity
rules.consensus_value: Sub-VL FIFO queue should only be read by one VL FIFO queue
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which mentions that 'A Sub-VL FIFO queue should only be read by one VL FIFO queue.' This matches the extracted rule exactly.
rules.test_hint: Configure a Sub-VL FIFO queue to be read by multiple VL FIFO queues and verify this configuration is rejected
rules.source_quote: A Sub-VL FIFO queue should only be read by one VL FIFO queue.

rules.name: VL MAC destination address identifier
rules.consensus_value: MAC destination address format for VL identifier
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly lists 'MAC destination address (VL identifier VLi)' as a parameter required on a per VL basis for configuring the Filtering, Policing, and Forwarding functions of the Switch. This matches the rule's description and constraint about the MAC destination address format for VL identifier.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid or malformed MAC destination addresses that don't match configured VL identifiers
rules.source_quote: MAC destination address (VL identifier VLi)

rules.name: VL bandwidth allocation gap
rules.consensus_value: per-VL bandwidth allocation gap configuration required
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly lists 'Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAGi)' as a parameter required for configuring the Filtering, Policing, and Forwarding functions of the Switch on a per-VL basis. This confirms the existence of the rule regarding the per-VL bandwidth allocation gap configuration.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on VLs with traffic rates that exceed the configured BAG limits
rules.source_quote: Bandwith Allocation Gap (BAGi)

rules.name: VL maximum allowed jitter
rules.consensus_value: per-VL maximum jitter constraint must be enforced
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions that the maximum allowed jitter on each VL at the output of the end-system should comply with certain formulas, and it is bounded at 500 μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network. This aligns with the rule's constraint that a per-VL maximum jitter constraint must be enforced.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with timing that exceeds the configured maximum jitter for a VL
rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Jitter

rules.name: VL account sharing configuration
rules.consensus_value: account can be shared or not shared
rules.justification: The rule regarding the 'ACcount (ACi)' specifying if an account is shared or not is explicitly mentioned in the specification text under the section '4.0 SWITCH SPECIFICATION'. It is listed as one of the parameters on a per VL basis, confirming that this is a genuine rule.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple VLs to use the same account when sharing is disabled, or violate account bandwidth limits
rules.source_quote: ACcount (ACi) [specifying if this account is shared or not]

rules.name: VL maximum ethernet frame size
rules.consensus_value: maximum allowed total ethernet line size per VL
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax)' as a parameter for both default reception and transmission VLs. This confirms that the rule regarding the maximum Ethernet frame size (Smax) is genuine and correctly extracted.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than the configured Smax for a VL
rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)

rules.name: VL minimum ethernet frame size
rules.consensus_value: minimum allowed total ethernet line size per VL
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)' as a parameter on a per VL basis within the switch configuration. This aligns with the rule extracted, confirming its validity.
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than the configured Smin for a VL
rules.source_quote: Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)

rules.name: VL priority classification
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Prioritization (high or low)' as a parameter on a per VL basis, which aligns with the rule's description of VL priority classification with allowed values 'high' and 'low'.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with priority markings that don't match the configured VL priority
rules.source_quote: Prioritization (high or low)

rules.name: Port maximum delay constraint
rules.consensus_value: per-port maximum delay limit must be enforced
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly states that an output port should not transmit frames that are older than 'max delay,' and the 'max delay' parameter is defined on a per-port basis in the configuration table. This aligns with the rule's description of a per-port maximum delay limit that must be enforced.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic patterns that cause port delays to exceed the configured maximum
rules.source_quote: Max delay

rules.name: Port operational state
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly lists 'Port State (ON/ OFF)' as a parameter required to configure the Filtering, Policing, and Forwarding functions of the Switch on a per port basis. This aligns with the rule extracted, confirming its validity.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to ports that are configured as OFF
rules.source_quote: Port State (ON/ OFF)

rules.name: Low priority VL output buffer size
rules.consensus_value: per-port output buffer size for low priority VLs must be configured
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Output Buffer Size for Low Priority VLs' as a parameter required to configure the Filtering, Policing, and Forwarding functions of the Switch. This aligns with the rule's description of configuring the output buffer size for low priority VLs.
rules.test_hint: Send bursts of low priority traffic that exceed the configured buffer size
rules.source_quote: Output Buffer Size for Low Priority VLs

rules.name: High priority VL output buffer size
rules.consensus_value: per-port output buffer size for high priority VLs must be configured
rules.justification: The specification text explicitly mentions 'Output Buffer Size for High Priority VLs' as a required parameter for configuring the switch's filtering, policing, and forwarding functions. This aligns with the rule's description of configuring the output buffer size for high priority VLs.
rules.test_hint: Send bursts of high priority traffic that exceed the configured buffer size
rules.source_quote: Output Buffer Size for High Priority VLs

rules.name: pin_programming_read_timing

The text clearly specifies that hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test.
rules.test_hint: Send initialization commands when Switch_Ground_Condition is false or attempt to read pins after Safety Test
rules.source_quote: Hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test (if any).

rules.name: pin_programming_flight_behavior
rules.consensus_value: When Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read and switch should use last memorized values
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 4.10.1.1. It specifies that when the Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read and the switch should use the last memorized values. This matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Force switch to read pin programming when Switch_Ground_Condition is false
rules.source_quote: When the Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read. The Switch should use the last memorized values.

rules.name: pin_count_requirement
rules.justification: The rule regarding the 12 program pins being checked by a parity bit is explicitly stated in the specification under section 4.10.1.2. The extracted value of 12 pins is correct as per the specification.
rules.test_hint: Configure switch with fewer or more than 12 program pins
rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.

rules.name: pin_programming_parity_check
rules.justification: The rule regarding the parity check for the 12 program pins (P1 to P12) is explicitly stated in the specification under section 4.10.1.2. The specification clearly mentions that these pins should be checked by a parity bit, which aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send pin programming data with incorrect parity
rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.

rules.name: pin_value_encoding
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 4.10.2.1, which describes the encoding of pin values for GROUND and OPEN states. The extracted values of 0 and 1 are correct according to the specification.
rules.test_hint: Send pin programming with values other than 0 or 1
rules.source_quote: GROUND value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 1. OPEN value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 0.

rules.name: Minimum Output Port Buffer Capacity
rules.justification: The rule regarding the minimum output port buffer capacity of 512 frames is explicitly stated in the specification text provided. The quote from the specification confirms that each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames, balanced between high and low priority.
rules.test_hint: Send more than 512 frames to a single output port simultaneously and verify switch can buffer them without dropping frames
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).

rules.name: Buffer Priority Balance
rules.consensus_value: Output port buffer capacity must be balanced between high and low priority frames

rules.test_hint: Fill output buffer with only high priority or only low priority frames and verify switch maintains proper priority balance
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).

rules.name: OPS mode functions
rules.consensus_value: in OPS mode, switch must perform frame filtering, traffic filtering, switching, and monitoring functions
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification mentions that in OPS mode, the switch performs operational functions including frame and traffic filtering, switching, and monitoring functions. This aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Verify that switches in OPS mode reject frames that violate filtering rules or policing constraints
rules.source_quote: In this mode, the Switch performs operational functions: frame and traffic filtering function, switching function, monitoring function, etc.

rules.name: Passive mode communication restriction
rules.consensus_value: in PASSIVE mode, switch only communicates with Network Management Function, all other functions stopped
rules.justification: The rule is directly supported by the specification text, which states that in PASSIVE MODE, the Switch only offers the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function and all other functions should be stopped.
rules.test_hint: Send normal traffic frames to a switch in PASSIVE mode and verify they are not forwarded
rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE MODE, the Switch only offers the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function), all others functions should be stopped

rules.name: Switch initialization before subscribers
rules.consensus_value: switches should be operational before their connected subscribers to allow subscriber communication during initialization
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly indicates that switches should be operational before their subscribers to allow communication during the initialization phase.
rules.source_quote: The Switches should be operational before their subscribers (connected LRUs), to allow subscribers to communicate via AFDX during their own initialization phase

rules.name: Fault indicator state during initialization
rules.consensus_value: during INIT mode, Fault/Healthy indicator must stay in Fault state
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 4.8.2.1 Initialization Sequence. The text clearly mentions that during INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state, which matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Monitor switch health indicators during initialization to verify they remain in fault state
rules.source_quote: During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state

rules.name: OPS mode normal functions requirement
rules.consensus_value: Switch must perform frames filtering, traffic policing, switching function, and end system function using activated OPS_Configuration_File data
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text, which describes the operational mode (OPS) of the switch. It specifies that in OPS mode, the switch should perform its normal functions such as frames filtering, traffic policing, switching function, and end system function, relying exclusively on the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Send frames when switch is in OPS mode but with invalid OPS_Configuration_File or when switch is not properly filtering/policing according to configuration
rules.source_quote: In OPS, the Switch should perform its normal functions (frames filtering and Traffic policing functions, Switching function, End System function) exclusively relying upon the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.

rules.name: OPS mode health indicator state
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under section 4.8.3, which mentions that in OPS mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state. The extracted value 'Healthy' is correct as per the specification.
rules.source_quote: In OPS mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.

rules.name: DL mode end system function configuration
rules.consensus_value: Switch must perform End System function using Default_Configuration_Table data exclusively
rules.justification: The specification text clearly states that in Dataloading mode (DL), the switch uses the Default_Configuration_File, which corresponds to the resident configuration. This aligns with the rule stating that the switch must perform its End System function using Default_Configuration_Table data exclusively in DL mode.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to switch in DL mode that require OPS_Configuration_File data instead of Default_Configuration_Table data
rules.source_quote: In DL Mode, the Switch should perform its End System function exclusively relying upon the data contained in its resident configuration table: Default_Configuration_Table.

rules.name: PASSIVE mode switch functions disabled
rules.consensus_value: All switch functions must be stopped and switch must remain silent
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification text which states that in PASSIVE MODE, all functions of the switch should be stopped except for the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function. This aligns with the rule's constraint that all switch functions must be stopped and the switch must remain silent.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to switch in PASSIVE mode and verify it does not forward, filter, or police them
rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE Mode, the functions of the Switch should be stopped and the switch should keep silent.

rules.name: PASSIVE mode network management communication
rules.consensus_value: Must maintain capability to communicate with Network Management Function using default VLs unless pin programming parity error
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text. The specification mentions that in PASSIVE Mode, the switch should maintain the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function using default VLs unless the passive state is due to an erroneous parity of the pin programming discretes.
rules.test_hint: Send network management frames to switch in PASSIVE mode and verify communication works on default VLs
rules.source_quote: Nevertheless, the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function should be maintained except if the passive state results from an erroneous parity of the pin programming discretes.

rules.name: QUIET mode frame forwarding prohibition
rules.consensus_value: Switch must not forward frames and must remain quiet (no message generation)
rules.justification: The rule is confirmed by the specification text, which clearly states that in QUIET mode, the switch will not forward frames and will remain quiet, not generating any messages. This aligns with the extracted rule's constraint.
rules.test_hint: Send frames through switch in QUIET mode and verify no forwarding or message generation occurs
rules.source_quote: The quiet mode ensures that the switch will not forward frames and will remain quiet (not try to generate a message).

rules.name: Delayed ACK timing
rules.justification: The rule regarding delayed ACK timing is explicitly stated in the specification text. The text clearly mentions that 'The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.' This matches the extracted rule, confirming its validity.
rules.test_hint: Test by delaying ACKs beyond 0.5 seconds and observe if the network reacts to the delay.
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.

rules.name: ACK every second full-size segment
rules.consensus_value: In a stream of full-sized segments, there should be an ACK for at least every second segment
rules.justification: The rule is explicitly stated in the specification text under the section 'GENERATING ACKNOWLEDGMENTS' on page 107. The specification mentions that in a stream of full-sized segments, there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment, which matches the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Test by sending multiple full-sized segments without sending ACKs for every second segment.
rules.source_quote: In a stream of full-sized segments there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment.

rules.name: Frame sequencing for simultaneous reception
rules.consensus_value: simultaneous frames must be sequenced for re-transmission
rules.justification: The rule regarding the sequencing of simultaneous frames for re-transmission is explicitly stated in the specification text. The source quote provided in the rule matches the relevant section of the specification, confirming the existence and correctness of the rule.
rules.test_hint: Send simultaneous frames to a switch and verify they are properly sequenced rather than dropped or corrupted
rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c

rules.name: switch forwarding based on MAC destination
rules.consensus_value: forwarding decision based on MAC destination field of received frames
rules.justification: The rule regarding switch forwarding based on the MAC destination is explicitly supported by the specification text. Table 3-2 in the specification clearly outlines that the forwarding decision is made based on the MAC destination field of received frames, which aligns with the extracted rule.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with different MAC destinations to verify switch forwards to correct output ports according to forwarding table
rules.source_quote: Switch Forwarding is defined in Table 3-2.

rules.name: Frame Filtering and Policing Order
